style_2_guidelines.guideline_authority: ACC/AHA Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure / ESC 2024

clinical_targets.goal: < 130/80 mmHg for non-elderly adults and high-risk patients
< 130–139/80 mmHg (avoid SBP < 120 or DBP < 70 mmHg if orthostatic symptoms)

steps_summary: Step 1: Initial Monotherapy vs. Initial Dual Combination
Step 3: Resistant Hypertension (Uncontrolled on 3 Agents Including Diuretic)

steps.title: Initial Monotherapy vs. Initial Dual Combination
steps.rationale: Stage 1 HTN (130–139 / 80–89 mmHg) with low CVD risk can start with monotherapy. Stage 2 HTN (BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg or > 20/10 mmHg over goal) should initiate with dual combination therapy, ideally as a Single-Pill Combination (SPC) to maximize adherence.

drug_classes.role: First-line class; superior renal and heart protection; first choice in diabetes or albuminuria.
drug_classes.dosing: Ramipril 2.5–10 mg daily; Enalapril 5–20 mg BID; Perindopril 5–10 mg daily.
drug_classes.pearls: Check serum K+ and creatinine within 1–2 weeks. Dry cough occurs in 5–15% (due to bradykinin); switch to ARB if cough develops.

drug_classes.role: First-line equivalent to ACEi with near-zero incidence of bradykinin-mediated cough.
drug_classes.dosing: Valsartan 80–320 mg daily; Losartan 50–100 mg daily; Telmisartan 40–80 mg daily.
drug_classes.pearls: NEVER combine ACEi and ARB (dual RAS blockade increases acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia without benefit).

drug_classes.role: Potent peripheral vasodilator; highly effective in elderly patients and isolated systolic hypertension.
drug_classes.dosing: Amlodipine 2.5–10 mg once daily; Lercanidipine 10–20 mg once daily.
drug_classes.pearls: Peripheral pedal edema is dose-dependent. Combining with an ACEi/ARB significantly reduces CCB-induced ankle edema.

drug_classes.role: Core component of combination therapy; thiazide-like agents (Indapamide) have longer half-life and superior CV trial evidence.
drug_classes.dosing: Indapamide 1.5–2.5 mg daily (or 1.5 mg SR); Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5–25 mg daily.
drug_classes.pearls: Monitor for hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and hyperuricemia (may trigger gout flares).

steps.title: Dual & Triple Therapy (Stepped Escalation)
steps.rationale: If blood pressure is uncontrolled on dual therapy, escalate to the golden triple regimen: A + C + D (RAS blocker + CCB + Diuretic).

drug_classes.role: Recommended triple therapy combining three complementary physiological mechanisms.
drug_classes.dosing: Available in Egyptian market as single-pill triple combinations (e.g. Amlodipine/Valsartan/HCTZ).
drug_classes.pearls: Controls BP in > 80% of patients when taken consistently.

steps.title: Resistant Hypertension (Uncontrolled on 3 Agents Including Diuretic)
steps.rationale: Confirm medication adherence and rule out white-coat effect or secondary causes. Add a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA).

drug_classes.role: Most effective fourth-line agent for resistant hypertension (PATHWAY-2 trial).
drug_classes.pearls: Safe only if serum potassium < 4.5 mEq/L and eGFR > 30 mL/min. Monitor K+ at 1, 4, and 12 weeks.

drug_classes.role: Reserve for patients with compelling cardiac indications (Post-MI, HFrEF, Angina, or Rate Control).
drug_classes.dosing: Bisoprolol 2.5–10 mg daily; Nebivolol (vasodilating beta-blocker) 5–10 mg daily.
drug_classes.pearls: Not recommended as initial monotherapy in uncomplicated hypertension without compelling cardiac disease.

pearls: Check serum K+ and creatinine within 1–2 weeks. Dry cough occurs in 5–15% (due to bradykinin); switch to ARB if cough develops.
NEVER combine ACEi and ARB (dual RAS blockade increases acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia without benefit).
Peripheral pedal edema is dose-dependent. Combining with an ACEi/ARB significantly reduces CCB-induced ankle edema.
Monitor for hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and hyperuricemia (may trigger gout flares).

special_populations.renal_impairment: ACEi/ARBs are first-line for albuminuria (UACR > 30 mg/g). Discontinue or lower diuretic if acute volume depletion occurs.
special_populations.pregnancy_lactation: ACEi, ARBs, and MRAs are strictly CONTRAINDICATED (teratogenic / fetotoxic). Safe first-line options: Methyldopa, Labetalol, or Nifedipine extended release.
special_populations.asthma: Avoid non-selective beta-blockers. Cardioselective beta-1 blockers (Bisoprolol, Nebivolol) or non-beta-blocker regimens preferred.

style_3_monograph.summary: A transient ischemic attack (TIA) is a stroke that lasts only a few minutes. It happens when the blood supply to part of the brain is briefly blocked. Symptoms of a TIA are like other stroke symptoms, but do not last as long. They happen suddenly, and include: Numbness or weakness, especially on one side of the body Confusion or trouble speaking or understanding speech Trouble seeing in one or both eyes Difficulty walking Dizziness Loss of balance or coordination Most symptoms of a TIA disappear within an hour, although they may last for up to 24 hours. Because you cannot tell if these symptoms are from a TIA or a stroke, you should go to the hospital right away. TIAs are often a warning sign for future strokes . Taking medicine, such as blood thinners , may reduce your risk of a stroke. Your doctor might also recommend surgery. You can also help lower your risk by having a healthy lifestyle . This includes not smoking, not drinking too much, eating a healthy diet, and exercising. It is also important to control other health problems, such as high blood pressure and cholesterol . NIH: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke
style_3_monograph.treatment: Consult healthcare provider for individualized management.
